summary: Slow completions and client-side timeouts when requesting very large max_tokens with deep system prompt
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated client-side HTTP timeouts and partial responses when creating completions with extremely large max_tokens (>=250k) coupled with a 40k+ token system prompt. Impact: Several customer production workflows (document drafting, long-format transformation) stalled, causing downstream job retries and billing concerns. Observed across multiple model variants and on the us-east serving fleet. Not a total outage but high business impact for the customer (enterprise SLA).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create POST /v1/completions request with model 'redwood-large-v1'. 2) Provide system prompt of ~45,000 tokens and set max_tokens = 260000. 3) Enable streaming=true and client-side timeout=90s. 4) Observe initial streaming chunks for ~30-60s then long gap and eventual client HTTP timeout at ~90s; sometimes final chunk arrives after 3-6 minutes as a late payload or the connection resets. Reproducible from two different VPC endpoints and from hosted API key.
expected_behavior: Continuous streaming with per-token throughput consistent with customer's baseline; request should either finish within reasonable SLO or be rejected with a 4xx/429 if budget too large, but should not cause long stalls leading to client timeouts and retries.
observed_behavior: Initial tokens stream normally, then server-side generation stalls for large periods (tens of seconds to minutes) before either resuming or terminating with 504/connection reset. Some requests resume and deliver full output after the client already retried, leading to duplicate invoices and confusion.
logs: Request IDs: rj-20260310-4b9a8f, rj-20260310-4b9a8f-2. NGINX upstream_read_timeout triggered in several traces. Runtime logs show 'context-window-spill: initiating cold-eviction' followed by 'prefetch-to-disk: start' and long blocking on '/mnt/kv-archive/snapshot-*.blk' reads. CPU utilization on the host remains moderate, but disk IO spikes correlate with stall windows. Attached sampled stack: runtime/main: finalizer_wait -> batch_scheduler: acquire_slot -> evict_manager: write_snapshot -> io: read_block (blocked).
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: very large token budgets are triggering background snapshotting of the attention cache to local disk which stalls the finalizer worker responsible for flushing generation buffers.
- SRE verified disk IO spikes on two hosts handling the customer's requests; the hosts are on EBS gp3 with baseline throughput; during spikes IO credit exhaustion observed.
- Scheduler logs indicate long 'acquire_slot' waits for finalizer threads when a large contiguous token allocation is present.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic request; forcing 'disable_kv_snapshot' flag removed stalls.
- Related to a recent change (runtime PR #2241) that added on-demand KV spill-to-disk for memory-heavy generations to avoid OOM across multi-tenant hosts. That PR's fallback path appears to block finalizer threads synchronously instead of offloading IO to async workers under heavy load.
- Customer reports invoice anomalies due to late completions that were billed as separate requests when client retried.
- Risk: other enterprise customers with heavy long-context usage might hit the same behavior under sustained load.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Thanks for reporting. Can you confirm whether this is only for streaming endpoints and whether non-streaming requests behave differently? Any example request IDs would be helpful.

Customer (LexiDraft SRE): We see it on both streaming and non-streaming calls; streaming shows the most visible client timeouts. Attached request ids and a flamegraph. We're on enterprise plan and need a workaround ASAP — this blocks nightly document ingestion.
Ravi Patel (On-call SRE): Marking P1. I reproduced locally and captured runtime logs. Opening investigation; temporarily throttling the customer's requests to avoid host IO saturation while we patch.

Engineering (Ana Gomez): Root cause candidate: PR #2241 uses synchronous spill and snapshot in the finalizer codepath. Patch proposal: make spill operations asynchronous and add per-request IO time budget; also fail-fast for max_tokens over configured cluster threshold. Working on a PR for a non-blocking spill worker.

Ravi Patel: Applied temporary mitigation at 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC — added admission-control rule that rejects max_tokens > 200k with 429 for affected cluster ring. Customer notified. Monitoring for recurrence.
Customer: A 429 is an acceptable temporary mitigation; please prioritize a permanent fix. Also request a billing adjustment for duplicate charges caused by retries.
resolution: Mitigation steps completed: 1) short-term: admission control rule deployed to reject requests with max_tokens > 200k on the us-east ring; customer notified and accepted. 2) mid-term: engineering merged runtime change (PR #2249) to offload KV snapshot IO to background async workers and impose per-request IO time budget; deployed canary to 5% of fleet on 2026-03-12. 3) long-term: implement request-level heuristics to recommend lower max_tokens and provide client-side SDK guardrails. Customer confirmed no new timeouts after admission control and accepted the planned patch. Billing team to review duplicate charges (ticket FIN-4122).
postmortem_followup:
- Track PR #2249 rollout and verify absent IO stall signals in the next 48 hours.
- Add explicit SDK warning for max_tokens > 100k and server-side suggestive error with recommended reduce-by percent.
- Create monitoring alert for 'finalizer_wait > 10s' with host-level IO saturation link.
- Finance to contact LexiDraft for reimbursement review.
